items.note: The lemma's content (forward invocation adds x_S to y_S for arbitrary scratch; three stages give (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restore every auxiliary) and all three proof steps (net change (JV+RG)x, bit and complex coefficients, stage composition) follow 741-765. But the network itself is never defined: the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection maps, the neighbour rules (|S∩T|=1 vs even intersection) and the eight schedule rows are only described by their three jobs, and J,V,R,G are left undefined.

States D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, and derives them by the paper's invariant: true at sources, preserved through a pointwise gate by R-linearity, continued to sinks.

Correctly states the nondegenerate labels in F^{⊗3}, nesting, the single decreasing edge per central wire (centre 3->4, loss h), L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, the ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and the telescoping argument. Missing: the gate-label table eq:motif-labels and the per-edge residual table that prove nesting and the dimension claims (A, P, B, Q are used without definition), and the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument (1073-1102).

States the matrices (P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at X_a sources, zero elsewhere), the frames Φ_M, the shear on every role and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. It follows the proof: rank of P_V-P_U equals the dimension change, the N rank-one exceptions 2P_{U_a}, then the endpoint difference I_m.

States the frames C_U, one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and the C^{⊗m} result after corrections. It follows the proof through weight additivity, odd weight giving the kernel, and the X_a->Y_a pair fixed by C=iZC^{-1}Z. It omits the step that the zero and full labels have frames I and C^{⊗m} (q_F=wt), which makes every other role telescope to C^{⊗m}. The k-column tensoring and the final negation and unexchange are also missing (1262-1314).
Has L/N<1/2, the deficit N-2L_b>0, s_c<W_c m, the exact η_b and η_c, η>20·2^{-50}, and log m<20, giving m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-η) and hence s/W<m^τ with τ=σ=1-2^{-50}. This is the paper's route.

Both lemmas are stated, and the controlled-shift lemma is derived as in the paper (split at Q-a and merge reversed, b^{O(1)} absorbed by the fibre, c increasing pieces, negation by stack). The elementary-streams lemma is only an infer step with no derivation (q^2-stream split, r=Wg+w row split, counter analysis at 513-550).

A=E_1 Π E_2 is derived by the paper's elimination (topmost row, rightmost pivot, every operation lower triangular). The shear cost follows: choice of the odd prime, O(V) triangular passes, conjugation, and one interchange per one of Π via D+=H, swap, D=H-D, giving exactly a recursive calls.

Follows the proof in full: the k=0 base case, the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Φ_{A_e} on each edge by matrix-shear, the frame identity with Φ_M, the endpoint Φ_{I_m}, the merge, and the three-update interchange. It then has s calls, F_k≤(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) summed geometrically to O(e^τ), and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule with the one-bit descriptor bound.

Follows the paper's route: peel ρ high digits so that R=q^{2ρ}≥W^k, pad to R', split e-ρ into base-m pieces handled by the power-width procedure with cost O(Ve^τ), then descriptor count, padding [2^u] to [q^e], and the one-bit unequal-width case.

Has every step of the paper: the frame change as a product of C_{v_j}, conjugation by P_M with the residual basis as the first columns of M, one child per slot, the inverse child via (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. The S0.1.5.3 method writes the scalar as β instead of b (minor slip).

Follows the proof: eight conditional updates flipping parity and restoring z, whole-chunk cyclic shifts, the bad set from the guard interval, δ_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting the bad set, swap-conjugated rotations, sorting repair, the last-bit XOR and the cost terms. The top claim gives O(V(L^τ+1)); the family conditions appear in S0.1.5.4.15. S0.1.5.4.3 slightly misdescribes the displacement and guard argument.

The route is the paper's: rows from the first q_0 chunks padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, rows split by u=Wg+w, F(e)≤(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^τ+1), overhead O(e^λ) from K≤e^{c/β}, geometric internal sum, leaf bound and base-m pieces. The top claim S0.1.5.6 says the result holds for any fixed λ'<1, whereas the paper needs max{λ,σ+β(1-σ)}<λ'<1; only S0.1.5.6.7 states that condition.

States the layer in O(Vd^{λ'}) with one truncation and error below √2·2^{-p}, and the Δ=⌈C_0 d^{C_1}⌉=o(p) guard width. Derives it as in 2450-2586 and 2686-2758: depth recurrence A(e)≤sA(e/m)+E, depth-to-size induction, εC_1<1, uniform packed costs, the layer identity and the row-sum-one truncation bound.

Covers character cancellation by the sign-changing shift, DIF rounds computing B_t F_t^-, the reverse procedure giving F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, and the layout L (prefix moves, at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges). It also has round order, layer cost per round, truncation commuting with J_E, error √2·ℓ·2^{-p}, and exact operators L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1}, all as in the paper.

Has B_0=2^{4p} evaluation, the separation |h_j|≤r2^{2p}<B_0/2, carries in {-1,0} and {0,1}, centred extraction, numerators ac-be and ae+bc, the negacyclic wrap, truncation by p+ℓ bits and the O(rp log(rp)) cost, in the paper's order.

Has the normalization check M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM), the identity P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error chain 2δ+η then 3δ+η then times M, giving √2·M(3ℓ+1)·2^{-p}, and the M=T/r products costing O(Tp log(rp)).

Derives the 1D identity as in the paper: N=CTD, the cited HvdH Gaussian facts, the Neumann inverse, and A=S' with B_0=D'J'C as contractions with normalizations 2^{-2α^2}. It then has the error and time table and the selection and Neumann costs, plus the tensor form with γ=2dα^2, linewise errors dp^2, line costs and O(Tpd^2(1+ℓ^τ)) axis exposure.

Has both identities with the paper's proof: periodicity of the chirp and the coefficient \bar a_j a_{j-k} \bar a_k=exp(2πi Σ s_i j_i k_i/t_i); the dilation identity giving R F^+ R=F^+, R commuting with pointwise products, the convolution normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2, and conjugation for F^+.

Has the fixed exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r and t_i, the comparison bands, α, γ and η with γ=o(b), the HvdH/Rosser-Schoenfeld prime count, disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T, α^4θ_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search, and the no-wraparound and capacity bounds, all as in the paper.

Has Φ as an algebra isomorphism, the triangular coordinates b_i=a_i+μ_i Σ_{j<i} a_j P_j, the descending update order, bijectivity on the padded box, the prefix-controlled cyclic shifts and the O(Tpd^2(1+ℓ^τ)) cost from O(d^2) axis moves.

Has well-definedness via (ζy)^r=1, the diagonal isomorphism, the wrap check ζ^{k+l}(-1)^h=ζ^j, and M_C=D_- ι^{-1} M_r(ι D_+ f, ι D_+ g)=(f*g)/T. The twist errors below 4 h_p each appear in S0.4.6.9.4.

Has the source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, 2^γ) with exact counterpart R F_s, F^+ by conjugation, and the six steps, with the two S scales undoing (u*v)/S^2. The top claim S0.4.6 says rescaling by S and 2^{2b+4}, while the paper's second scale is 2^{2b+4}S; S0.4.6.7 and S0.4.6.8 state it correctly.

Follows the paper's error chain: E_ring<5TL, convolution <6TL, chirp <8TL, E_s=9·2^γ TL, product (2E_s+2), opposite (3E_s+2), E_w<28·2^γ T^2 L, final <448b·2^{-b+γ}≤448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2. It keeps the disk margins and finishes with rounding, the capacity bound and the carry recurrence to 2n bits.

Has V=Tp, the seven normalized rows justified individually, the margins g_1..g_7 with min=2^{-181}=2κ, setup and exceptional sorting o(V), log p powers absorbed by p^κ, O(n(log n)^{1-κ}), and the schoolbook cutoff, as in 4808-4995.

S0 only asserts that the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It never gives the eventual lower bound T_A(n)≥c_A n lg n, its negation via liminf, or the observation that the power saving gives limit zero.

errors.says: Method: use the Frankl-Wilson style form <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1 on indicator vectors.
errors.paper: The form x^T(I-J/9)y on Q^h is used for the bit network only; the complex network uses F_2^h with the ordinary dot product. The paper credits the intersection formulas to Alon's construction, not Frankl-Wilson.

errors.says: Method: use the one-bit identity H_0=βSCS coordinatewise.
errors.paper: H_0=b S C S with b=(1-i)/2, giving H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. In the paper β denotes the cutoff exponent 1/2, so H_0=βSCS would be false.

errors.says: Each coordinate moves by at most four, so with ten guard values on either side no segment leaves its quotient range.
errors.paper: The displacement is at most four (eight suffices) 'even if an intermediate point leaves its starting quotient square'. Off the bad set, the guard interval 10≤g≤2^{K-1}-11 keeps each segment inside [0,2^K-1], so no segment carries or borrows.

errors.says: The recurrence sums to O(d^{λ'}) over the base-m pieces for any fixed λ'<1.
errors.paper: The bound O(d^{λ'}) holds for fixed λ' with max{λ,σ+β(1-σ)}<λ'<1, not for every λ'<1. S0.1.5.6.7 states this correctly.

errors.says: ... the opposite-sign transform, rescaling by S and 2^{2b+4}, rounding ...
errors.paper: Step 4 multiplies by S and step 5 by 2^{2b+4}S, so the total scale is 2^{2b+4}S^2 (the two S undo different normalizations). S0.4.6.7 and S0.4.6.8 state this correctly.

chain: The tree reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-κ}) by the paper's route: the bank-exchange network with frames, labels and the rank budget s<Wm (τ=σ=1-2^{-50}) drives both fast procedures (address interchange and simultaneous butterfly layer); these feed synthetic transforms and convolution, Gaussian resampling with Bluestein's chirp and the retained permutations, CRT and twist, the six-step algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table with minimum margin 2κ. It thins in the finite-network construction, where the gate maps, neighbour rules, N, m=h^3, the gate-label and residual tables and the binary orthonormal-basis argument appear only as quoted conclusions. It also thins in the complex phase interface (the zero and full label frames are omitted) and in the conjecture refutation, which S0 only asserts.

steps.note: The fixed linear network sending (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every auxiliary wire is stated and derived, over three-element subsets of [100] with the m-dimensional F^{⊗3}. However N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given explicitly, and N is used without definition.
Has the common frame commuting with the pointwise gate, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the point that intermediate frames are free to make edges cheap.
Has nondegenerate labels in the m-dimensional F^{⊗3}, edges joining comparable labels, and the central-wire 3->4 edges as the only decreasing ones, each losing h. The label table itself is not given.
P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U; the N source edges 2P_{U_a} are the rank-one exceptions.
Has Σ|Δdim|=Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich via telescoping, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
Has L/N=100/539 and 101/539, both below 1/2, the deficit N-2L_b>0, and s_c<W_c m.
Has P_{U_a^⊥}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m at X_a and zero source with identity sink elsewhere, so every row receives H<-H+D.
Has A=E_1 Π E_2, exactly a interchanges plus O(V), each interchange a recursive call, so s calls per node.
Has children of volume V/W, F_k≤(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^τ with τ=1-2^{-50} from η>20·2^{-50} and log m<20, giving F_k=O(e^τ).

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed with their defining quantities and in their chain roles: network, frames, labels, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, budget, strict deficit, endpoint identity, rank-a shears as recursive calls, and the recurrence with τ=1-2^{-50}. The only thin spot is C1, where the sizes N=binom(100,3)^3 and m=100^3 and the gate definitions are not written out.
